mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates more in-person commuting, which should lift retail visits within four weeks as workers make more weekday purchase trips after leaving home.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain above their t-2w levels.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility keeps falling while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated, households are spending more time outside home on routine errands, which should shift some discretionary trips into retail and recreation over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below its t-3w level and GROCERY_PHARM remains above -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or lower over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays below the prior three-week average and GROCERY_PHARM stays relatively elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in PARKS mobility signals broader leisure normalization and warmer-weather outdoor activity spillovers, which should pull retail and recreation higher over the next four weeks through companion outings and shopping after park visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days despite PARKS holding above its t-1w level and trending upward for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop sharply together, it reflects mobility restriction or renewed caution, and retail and recreation should weaken within one week because fewer commuters generate fewer incidental shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its last-4-week average after simultaneous week-on-week declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility below baseline indicates more time spent outside the home, and that reallocation should first appear in retail and recreation within two weeks as households resume discretionary outings.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 11 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL remains below 11 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while RETAIL_REC is still depressed, the same trip-chaining behavior that supports essential shopping will spill into nearby discretionary retail, producing a small positive change in retail and recreation over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its recent four-week mean even as GROCERY_PHARM continues to trend upward or stays above -10.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with easing workplace and transit suppression is a seasonal reactivation pattern; as outdoor and commuting activity normalize together, retail and recreation should rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each improve week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all improve together.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL keeps easing and TRANSIT continues recovering from a low base, the city is moving back toward normal circulation, which should keep retail and recreation above its last-month level over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT continues to recover from its recent trough.
